title: Review QML and C++ for simplicity and establish KISS-based coding guidelines
scope: Selected after DEV-005. Use Google C++ Style Guide as a critically assessed base and review QML one file at a time, tracing definitions and all instantiation points. No-change findings are valid. Keep the guide a working draft while source review is incomplete.
request: KISS is important to the user. Analyze both the QML and C++ code and establish project coding guidelines based on that analysis.
expected: A practical, concise CODING_GUIDELINES.md grounded in QShopper's actual code and Qt usage, with simplicity as a central decision criterion.
review_topics: Review project-owned QML components, C++ sources/headers, and relevant tests, identifying both straightforward patterns worth retaining and unnecessary complexity.
Assess responsibilities, dependencies, state flow, naming, component/class boundaries, and whether abstractions reduce or increase the effort needed to understand the code.
For QML, review bindings versus imperative updates, property/signal interfaces, theme usage, gesture/state handling, visual parenting, component reuse, and avoidable duplicated behavior.
For C++, review Qt ownership/lifetimes, model/view contracts, persistence boundaries, error handling, public interfaces, and opportunities to simplify control flow without weakening correctness.
Identify obsolete or unused code and workarounds, establishing their purpose before recommending removal.
Distinguish useful reuse from generic frameworks or helper layers that make a small application harder to follow.
guideline_principles: Prefer clear, direct, idiomatic Qt code that solves the current requirement.
Introduce abstraction, indirection, or generalization only when it makes the real code simpler to understand and maintain.
Do not equate KISS with the fewest lines, dense expressions, or removing necessary safety and error handling.
Remove duplication when the resulting shared code is simpler overall; avoid turning small similarities into an unnecessary framework.
Preserve DESIGN.md's deliberate product behavior and explain necessary complexity rather than simplifying away required interactions.
Keep the guidelines specific enough to guide real changes and short enough to consult regularly.
implementation_notes: Base recommendations on cited project examples and supported Qt/C++20 practices; avoid imposing a generic style guide without analyzing this codebase.
Coordinate formatting guidance with DEV-002/DEV-003, build simplicity with DEV-004, and analyzer guidance with DEV-005 instead of duplicating or contradicting their configuration.
Separate mechanical formatting rules from architectural, correctness, and maintainability guidance.
Capture proposed refactors as separate backlog work rather than performing a broad rewrite while writing the guide.
Link the resulting guide from AGENTS.md once it exists.
acceptance_criteria: Review both QML and C++ and record representative findings with project file references.
Create CODING_GUIDELINES.md with practical language-specific guidance and shared KISS principles grounded in those findings.
Include concrete examples or decision criteria for when an abstraction helps and when direct code is preferable.
Make the guidance consistent with product design, Qt model/ownership requirements, formatting choices, and the supported build workflow.
List actionable simplification candidates separately and retain justified complexity.
Update AGENTS.md to point future contributors to the completed guide; no functional changes should be bundled into the review/documentation task.
Assess Google C++ guide rules against Qt, KISS and established project conventions, recording reasons for adaptations rather than blindly importing policy.
Review QML sequentially with definition/use-site geometry responsibilities and valid no-change outcomes recorded.
evidence: User emphasized KISS and requested QML/C++ analysis leading to coding guidelines during backlog gathering on 2026-10-28.
user_direction: Use https://google.github.io/styleguide/cppguide.html as the C++ base, without accepting every rule at face value.
Progress one QML file at a time and review both its definition and instantiation points, including implicit sizes at definition and width/height/Layout/anchors at use sites.
It is acceptable that no changes are needed.
Prefer Layout variants over Row/Column positioners for new/revised layout composition.
During IconButton review, replace its contentItem Item/manual positioning with a Layout and honor inherited button display modes.
Continue reviewing sequentially without stopping at each no-change file; stop at the first concrete KISS improvement for discussion. Keep verification and notes proportionate.
Keep the three explicit Dark/Light/System theme buttons in View; user declined replacing them with a Repeater.
Keep SortFilterProxyModel parser-status hooks and current initialization phase; user declined moving their setup to the constructor. DEV-007 remains separate.
For test assets, fix review findings directly without asking for approval of each test-only change (2026-11-03).
review_method: Trace base types, content, derived components, delegates, Loaders, dynamic creation and test instantiations.
Record actual sizing and positioning ownership on both axes and consider padding, insets, font/text, state and scale dependencies.
Record keep/change/no-change decisions with evidence; reading a caller is not completion of that caller review.
Keep suspected bugs, confirmed bugs, simplification candidates and validation gaps distinct. Do not bundle functional fixes into the documentation review.
